# **Architecture Specification for MuniAudit-AI: Multimodal Municipal Public Works Verification Engine**

The optimal system architecture for MuniAudit-AI resolves a critical vulnerability in municipal public works administration: the systemic failure to verify desilting claims across disconnected physical, spatial, and documentary artifacts1. For a three-to-four-day hackathon, the system must be constructed as a **Modular Monolith** running within a unified application runtime backed by a single spatial database (PostgreSQL with PostGIS) and an embedded asynchronous task broker. This design eliminates distributed transaction overhead, network serialization latency, and deployment complexity while strictly isolating domain boundaries4. For enterprise production, the architecture must transition to a **Workflow Orchestration Architecture** anchored by a durable state machine engine (such as Temporal) paired with an **Event-Driven Ingestion Backbone** (Apache Kafka), dedicated machine learning inference workers, and an append-only cryptographic audit ledger6.

MuniAudit-AI operates conceptually as a dual-engine deterministic-probabilistic reconciliation pipeline. The system enforces physical, geometric, and statutory invariants—material density limits, kinematic transit feasibility, cadastral boundary containment, and commercial vehicle identity verifications—as non-negotiable legal gatekeepers2. Machine learning models are strictly bounded to perceptual feature extraction, layout-aware optical character recognition, and cross-temporal visual deduplication1. Downstream, a Dempster-Shafer evidential reasoning engine synthesizes probabilistic inference with hard rule violations, explicitly modeling epistemic uncertainty and evidentiary conflict rather than generating opaque, uncalibrated risk probabilities12.

In municipal governance, automated payment authorization is an architectural anti-pattern8. MuniAudit-AI functions strictly as an evidential triage and decision-support engine. It systematically isolates widespread procurement fraud vectors—such as "ghost trips," vehicle identity spoofing, photographic recycling across fiscal years, and gravimetric-volumetric dissonance—and compiles verified discrepancy dossiers for human review1. By maintaining an immutable chain of custody from raw pixel ingestion to final certified PDF export, the architecture provides statutory defensibility before municipal vigilance commissions, state comptrollers, and public accounts committees17.

## **System Boundaries and Operational Actors**

The operational boundary of MuniAudit-AI defines the perimeter of analytical verification, separating internal auditing mechanisms from external municipal enterprise systems, edge hardware, and banking channels.

The internal system boundary encapsulates all functions required to ingest, normalize, analyze, fuse, and review municipal billing evidence. This includes the validation of raw evidence files (photographs, weighbridge dockets, scanned Measurement Books, driver trip sheets, and contractor invoices), feature extraction pipelines, spatial trajectory reconstruction, deterministic business rule verification, multimodal evidence fusion, and human auditor review workflows2. The boundary terminates externally at integration interfaces: signed webhooks emitted to municipal Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) databases for payment disbursement, spatial query interfaces connected to municipal Geographic Information System (GIS) cadastres, and secure lookups against national transport registries2. Edge sensors (such as automated weighbridge load cells, closed-circuit television cameras, and vehicle telematics units) and municipal banking disbursement engines remain entirely outside the system boundary8.

System actors interact with MuniAudit-AI through role-based access boundaries that enforce statutory separation of duties:

&nbsp;

| Actor Role | Administrative Domain | Primary System Interactions | Threat Model & Risk Vectors |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Contractor / Vendor** | External Commercial Entity | Submits raw billing dossiers, invoices, weighbridge dockets, trip logs, and site imagery via upload interfaces. | Photographic recycling across contracts, metadata spoofing, OCR manipulation, payload inflation1. |
| **Junior Engineer (JE) / Site Inspector** | Municipal Field Administration | Records physical trench measurements (![][image1]) in the Measurement Book (MB), uploads field verification imagery, and signs site completion certificates3. | Collusion with vendors, fictitious measurement entries, off-site photo capture outside drain corridors2. |
| **Executive Engineer (EE)** | Municipal Approval Authority | Reviews automated risk summaries, inspects flagged discrepancies, evaluates technical explanations, and issues administrative approvals3. | Administrative rubber-stamping, unverified override approvals, pressure to disburse funds against uninspected work24. |
| **Municipal Auditor / Vigilance Officer** | Independent Oversight (Internal/CAG) | Conducts statutory audits, inspects visual-spatial discrepancies, drills down into raw evidence, and signs formal investigation reports17. | Access-token compromise, selective omission of audit findings, delayed reporting past dispute windows20. |
| **System Administrator** | Municipal Information Technology | Manages spatial cadastres, configures physical density parameters, sets model confidence thresholds, and oversees system health. | Unauthorized parameter relaxation (e.g., loosening density thresholds), audit log truncation, unauthorized role grants10. |

## **Fourteen-Tier Functional Architecture Specification**

The functional architecture organizes MuniAudit-AI into fourteen technology-independent layers, progressing from raw evidentiary intake to statutory report compilation.

### **1\. Ingestion Layer**

The Ingestion Layer provides secure, rate-limited intake interfaces for heterogeneous billing packages. It accepts multipart file bundles containing raster imagery (JPEG, PNG, TIFF), document scans (PDF), tabular trip summaries (CSV, XLSX), and telematics breadcrumbs (GeoJSON, GPX). The layer enforces cryptographic integrity immediately upon arrival: each file is scanned against magic-byte signatures to block MIME spoofing, passed through antivirus inspection filters, and assigned a SHA-256 cryptographic digest. Files are written to an isolated quarantine partition within the object store, and an EvidenceBundleReceived event containing the manifest of file URIs and checksums is emitted.

### **2\. Evidence Normalization Layer**

Heterogeneous evidence must be converted into canonical domain representations before downstream processing. The Evidence Normalization Layer parses raw artifacts into structured schemas validated against strict schema specifications. Spatial coordinates extracted from EXIF metadata, GPS logs, or manual survey entries are transformed from local municipal grids or diverse coordinate systems into standard WGS84 (EPSG:4326). Timestamps across weighbridge slips, photo EXIF headers, and vehicle tracking logs are standardized to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) with explicit timezone offset preservation. Vehicle registration strings are parsed through regular expressions conforming to national transport standards to eliminate syntactic formatting anomalies (such as spacing or punctuation variations).

### **3\. Feature Extraction Layer**

This layer extracts geometric, textual, and perceptual signals from normalized artifacts:

* *Document Feature Extraction*: Scanned Measurement Books and weighbridge dockets undergo layout analysis and optical character recognition (OCR) to extract tabular line items, net and tare weights, serial numbers, operational dates, and signature bounding boxes3.  
* *Visual Feature Extraction*: Pre-desilting and post-desilting site imagery is processed to generate 64-bit perceptual hashes (pHash) for near-duplicate identification, deep convolutional embeddings for semantic retrieval, and EXIF extraction (focal length, exposure, solar azimuth, and device serial numbers)11.  
* *Spatial Feature Extraction*: GPS telematics time series are matched to road network graphs to compute trip distances, point-to-point transit times, and dwell intervals. Municipal GIS drain polylines are buffered by administrative corridor widths (e.g., 15 meters) to create spatial containment polygons.

### **4\. Machine Learning Inference Layer**

The Machine Learning Inference Layer executes specialized probabilistic models:

* *Silt Segmentation and Volume Estimation*: Computer vision segmentation models evaluate paired before-and-after photographs to detect the presence of standing silt, water volume, and post-clearance bedrock or concrete canal lining.  
* *Cross-Temporal Image Deduplication*: A high-dimensional vector search index compares newly submitted image embeddings against historical municipal image databases spanning previous fiscal years and adjacent municipal wards, exposing cross-contract photographic recycling1.  
* *Document Tamper Detection*: Neural models inspect weighbridge dockets and invoice scans for font splicing, inconsistent character kerning, localized digital noise variance, and duplicated document serial numbers.  
* *Kinematic Anomaly Profiler*: Evaluates trip velocity distributions against historical traffic baselines, flagging synthetic GPS trajectories or physically implausible transit intervals2.

### **5\. Deterministic Validation Layer**

Operating as an unbypassable gatekeeper, this layer evaluates non-negotiable physical laws, civil engineering standards, and administrative procurement rules6. A claim failing a deterministic rule receives an immediate violation flag regardless of ML model outputs.

The physical mass-volume validation checks that recorded excavation volumes match aggregate weighbridge weights3. The recorded volume ![][image2] from the Measurement Book (![][image3]) is converted to an expected mass range using standard wet silt bulk density bounds (![][image4] to ![][image5])3:

![][image6]

![][image7]

where ![][image8] represents an allowable 15% environmental moisture variance. If the cumulative net weight registered across all weighbridge dockets (![][image9]) falls outside this envelope, a deterministic gravimetric violation is raised.

Additional deterministic checks include:

* *Vehicle Classification Integrity*: Automated cross-referencing of license plate numbers against national transport databases (e.g., VAHAN), verifying that registered vehicle types correspond to heavy commercial tippers or dump trucks, immediately flagging two-wheelers, auto-rickshaws, or passenger vehicles billed for silt haulage2.  
* *Spatial Geofence Containment*: Photographic EXIF GPS coordinates must fall within a 15-meter corridor of the contracted municipal drain polyline, and dumping coordinates must fall within authorized disposal facility boundaries25.  
* *Weighbridge Arithmetic*: The internal mathematics of every slip must satisfy ![][image10] exactly, with timestamps falling strictly within the contracted execution period.  
* *Kinematic Feasibility*: Point-to-point transit times between the desilting corridor and the designated disposal site must satisfy ![][image11], flagging "ghost trips" executed at physically impossible speeds or with instantaneous roundtrip returns2.

### **6\. Multimodal Evidence Fusion Layer**

This layer synthesizes deterministic rule violations with probabilistic ML inference outputs. Rather than utilizing an uncalibrated, black-box deep neural network, the layer implements **Dempster-Shafer Evidence Theory** to combine independent belief masses over the frame of discernment ![][image12]12.

Each evidence source ![][image13] provides a basic probability assignment (mass) ![][image14] satisfying ![][image15], where ![][image16] represents epistemic uncertainty (e.g., missing data, degraded image resolution, or partial GPS coverage)13. The orthogonal sum combines independent evidence sources (vision inference, spatial containment, kinematic profile, gravimetric consistency):

![][image17]

The normalization factor ![][image18] measures the degree of mutual conflict across the evidence sources14:

![][image19]

When ![][image18] exceeds a configured threshold (e.g., ![][image20]), the system identifies an *Evidentiary Contradiction* (such as high visual silt presence contradicted by zero corresponding weighbridge mass). In this scenario, the claim is assigned a high Composite Risk Score (![][image21]) and prioritized for human audit review, rather than allowing contradictory signals to cancel each other out12.

### **7\. Explainability Layer**

The Explainability Layer translates internal mathematical tensors, rule violation bitmasks, and Dempster-Shafer belief distributions into natural-language audit narratives and visual inspection artifacts6. It generates:

* Side-by-side visual diff panels highlighting spatial offsets between claimed photo coordinates and actual drain polylines.  
* Document inspection overlays rendering green and red bounding boxes directly over scanned weighbridge slips to highlight arithmetic errors, font splices, or duplicated docket IDs.  
* A tabular discrepancy manifest that itemizes each breached municipal manual clause, the observed value, the permissible statutory threshold, and the financial impact on the total invoice value3.

### **8\. Audit Workflow Layer**

The Audit Workflow Layer governs the operational lifecycle of every billing dossier through an explicit Finite State Machine (FSM). The FSM enforces legal non-repudiation and state transitions:

Transition guards prevent illegal operations: a claim with an unresolved deterministic violation cannot transition to CERTIFIED\_APPROVED without an explicit, cryptographically signed administrative override from the Executive Engineer7.

### **9\. Persistence Layer**

The Persistence Layer implements a polyglot storage architecture tailored to municipal audit requirements:

* *Object Storage*: WORM-compliant (Write Once, Read Many) distributed storage for raw and normalized evidentiary files (PDFs, TIFFs, raw images).  
* *Relational Spatial Database*: PostgreSQL with PostGIS extensions to manage structured claim metadata, municipal drain vector layers, cadastral boundaries, contractor registries, and normalized document line items.  
* *Immutable Audit Ledger*: An append-only cryptographic log that records every state transition, rule evaluation, ML inference score, and user interaction. Each log entry incorporates a SHA-256 hash chaining back to the previous entry, providing verifiable proof against database tampering9.

### **10\. Notification Layer**

An asynchronous notification router that dispatches operational alerts based on workflow state transitions. It emits signed webhook payloads to municipal ERP systems when claims are certified or rejected, dispatches SMS and email alerts to Executive Engineers when claims are flagged for critical discrepancies, and populates auditor task queues with prioritized review dockets.

### **11\. Human Review Layer**

A dual-pane web-based review console for municipal auditors and vigilance officers8. The interface integrates:

* An interactive GIS viewport rendering contracted drain corridors, dumping ground boundaries, vehicle breadcrumb trails, and photographic capture locations.  
* An evidentiary document inspector displaying high-resolution scans, extracted OCR tables, and automated field annotations.  
* An interactive override panel where authorized engineers must input a structured, statutory justification before clearing any system flag, with mandatory digital certificate signing7.

### **12\. Report Generation Layer**

The final layer compiles the complete evidentiary audit chain into an immutable, statutory-grade PDF/A document and an accompanying JSON-LD compliance manifest18. The generated audit report embeds:

* Executive billing summary and invoice itemization.  
* Deterministic rule pass/fail logs with civil engineering calculations3.  
* Visual evidence exhibits, including side-by-side photographic comparisons, spatial buffer maps, and OCR discrepancy highlights.  
* The complete chronological audit ledger, including auditor identities, timestamps, override justifications, and PKI digital signatures (X.509) ensuring non-repudiation in judicial or vigilance proceedings9.

## **Synchronous Versus Asynchronous Architectural Boundaries**

A critical requirement in enterprise audit design is the separation of synchronous, latency-critical operations from asynchronous, long-running computational pipelines. Attempting to execute heavy computer vision models or fragile external API calls within a synchronous HTTP request-response cycle leads to connection pool exhaustion, client timeouts, and cascading system failures.

| Operational Domain | Trigger / Endpoint | SLA Target | Concurrency & Isolation Model | Failure Strategy |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Synchronous Domain** | POST /dossier/upload-ticket | ![][image34]ms | Stateless API worker; generates pre-signed upload URL. | Fail-fast with HTTP 400/503; client retries. |
| **Synchronous Domain** | GET /claims/{id}/audit-dossier | ![][image39]ms | Read-only replica query; pre-compiled JSON payload. | Return cached view or 504 on replica lag. |
| **Synchronous Domain** | POST /claims/{id}/lock | ![][image37]ms | Distributed atomic lease acquisition in Redis. | HTTP 409 Conflict if locked by another auditor. |
| **Synchronous Domain** | POST /claims/{id}/adjudicate | ![][image40]ms | Transactional ACID row update with state machine guard. | Rollback transaction on constraint violation. |
| **Asynchronous Domain** | EvidenceBundleReceived event | ![][image41]s | Distributed normalization workers; Celery/Temporal queue. | Retry with exponential backoff up to 3 times; quarantine on failure. |
| **Asynchronous Domain** | ExtractDocumentFeatures task | ![][image42]s | Dedicated GPU worker pool; partitioned document queues. | Emit partial OCR output with low confidence flags; dead-letter queue. |
| **Asynchronous Domain** | ExecuteVisionInference task | ![][image43]s | Dedicated GPU worker pool; batched inference processing. | Flag image as unprocessable; log error to claim. |
| **Asynchronous Domain** | QueryTransportRegistry task | ![][image44]s | Rate-limited I/O worker pool; external API connector. | Circuit breaker trips on repeated timeouts; route to retry queue. |
| **Asynchronous Domain** | CompileSignedAuditReport task | ![][image45]s | Sandboxed CPU workers; isolated memory limits. | Log rendering failure; alert administrator; retry via dead-letter queue. |

Synchronous interfaces are strictly reserved for lightweight user operations: initiating an upload session, retrieving pre-compiled audit dossiers, acquiring a claim review lock, and submitting final human adjudication decisions with digital signatures7. These endpoints maintain an SLA of under 500 milliseconds and perform zero heavy computation.

All computational, parsing, computer vision, deterministic verification, external network queries, and document compilation tasks are pushed across an asynchronous boundary managed by persistent message queues or workflow activity tasks. When a contractor uploads an evidence bundle, the gateway immediately acknowledges receipt with a tracking identifier and enqueues a background job. As individual workers complete OCR parsing, visual feature extraction, and vehicle registry lookups, they update the claim's feature set and trigger downstream rule execution asynchronously. This ensures that slow third-party APIs (such as government transport portals) or compute-intensive deep learning tasks never degrade the responsiveness of the auditor workbench2.

## **Comparative Evaluation of Architectural Paradigms**

Selecting the correct architecture requires evaluating delivery speed, operational complexity, audit non-repudiation, and lifecycle management across four candidate paradigms:

&nbsp;

| Evaluation Dimension | Modular Monolith | Microservices Architecture | Event-Driven Architecture (EDA) | Workflow Orchestration Architecture |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Implementation Complexity** | **Lowest**: Single repository, unified database migrations, local debugging, zero network serialization. | **Very High**: Multiple container repositories, service mesh, API gateways, distributed tracing, complex CI/CD. | **High**: Requires broker management, consumer group balancing, schema registries, and dead-letter queues. | **Medium**: Requires state machine server (Temporal/Camunda), worker pools, and workflow definition management. |
| **Hackathon Feasibility (3–4 Days)** | **Optimal**: Fast iterative prototyping; in-memory data passing; single Docker Compose environment. | **Unfeasible**: Setup overhead, RPC interface definitions, and deployment friction consume available development time. | **Sub-optimal**: Broker infrastructure setup and event choreography consume excessive time; difficult to debug locally. | **Acceptable but Tight**: Orchestration SDK learning curves and worker setups introduce unnecessary friction for a prototype. |
| **Audit Trail Non-Repudiation** | **Medium**: Relies on application-level transactional database logging; single database vulnerability. | **Low-Medium**: Audit trails are fragmented across services; requires distributed log aggregation to reconstruct history. | **High**: Append-only event stream naturally captures historical transitions, but state reconstruction requires replay logic. | **Highest**: Native deterministic replay, execution DAG visualization, immutable state histories, guaranteed execution6. |
| **Human-in-the-Loop Handling** | **Poor**: Requires custom polling loops, brittle database flags, and complex custom cron schedulers. | **Poor**: Long-running sagas across services are difficult to coordinate; manual intervention points create zombie states. | **Moderate**: Coordinated via compensation events and timeout queues, but lacks centralized visibility into paused states. | **Native**: First-class support for durable timers, human task waiting (days/months), state suspension, and resume hooks7. |
| **Fault Isolation & Partial Failure** | **Low**: Memory leaks or crashes in compute-heavy OCR or Vision workers can bring down the entire application runtime. | **Highest**: Failure in an OCR worker has zero impact on the Ingestion Gateway or Auditor Workbench. | **High**: Consumers fail independently; unprocessed events remain durably buffered on message broker partitions. | **High**: Workflow engine retries failed activities with exponential backoff; workflow execution state remains safely persisted. |
| **Horizontal Scalability** | **Limited**: Entire monolithic runtime must be scaled uniformly; cannot scale GPU workers independently of API layer. | **Targeted**: GPU-bound vision services and I/O-bound gateways scale on independent auto-scaling policies. | **Targeted**: Consumers scale independently based on topic partition depth and consumer lag metrics. | **Targeted**: Activity worker pools scale independently based on task queue depths and hardware profiles (CPU vs GPU). |

### **Paradigm Verdict for Hackathon and Production**

For a **3–4 day hackathon**, the **Modular Monolith** is the definitively superior pattern. Implementing microservices or complex distributed event brokers during a 72-hour window introduces excessive failure modes: CORS configuration errors, container networking bugs, uncoordinated schema migrations, and complex deployment chains. A Modular Monolith allows a team to focus 100% of its engineering capacity on the core analytical problem—reconciling multi-source billing evidence—while maintaining clean logical separation of concerns within a single codebase4.

For **enterprise production**, the system must transition to a **Workflow Orchestration Architecture** paired with an **Event-Driven Ingestion Backbone**. Municipal public works auditing is characterized by inherently long-running, asynchronous business processes: claims frequently pause for weeks while awaiting site inspections, laboratory silt sample reports, or administrative drill-downs3. Managing these extended lifecycles via ad-hoc database flags in a traditional monolith leads to brittle polling architectures and unrecoverable states upon node failure. A workflow orchestration engine (such as Temporal) provides durable execution guarantees, automatic retry policies, visual state tracking, and native human-in-the-loop task routing required for statutory municipal oversight7.

## **Minimal Deployable Architecture for a Three-to-Four-Day Hackathon**

The hackathon architecture maximizes development speed and operational stability by packaging the entire system into a single application runtime supported by two standard infrastructure containers, executing locally or on a single virtual machine.

### **Deployment Layout and Technology Selection**

The hackathon runtime is structured as a unified Python application utilizing FastAPI, organized internally into strict domain packages: ingestion, normalization, extraction, rules, fusion, audit, and reporting. Background task execution is handled by an embedded Celery worker pool connected to a local Redis container, eliminating the need for external workflow clusters.

The storage tier is consolidated into a single PostgreSQL 16 container with the PostGIS extension enabled. Evidence files (scanned PDFs, photographs) are stored directly on a mounted local Docker volume (/data/artifacts/), with relative file paths recorded in the database. The user interface is implemented as a unified server-rendered application using FastAPI templates (Jinja2, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet.js for GIS rendering), completely avoiding the overhead of configuring separate frontend single-page applications, CORS proxies, and token exchange flows.

&nbsp;

| Production Architecture Component | Hackathon Pragmatic Substitute | Velocity Justification & Operational Trade-off |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Distributed Object Store (S3/MinIO)** | Local Filesystem Mounted Directory (/data/artifacts/) | Eliminates bucket permission setup, S3 SDK credential debugging, and upload latency. Files are accessed via local POSIX calls. |
| **High-Performance Routing Engine (OSRM)** | Haversine Distance with 1.414 Road-Tortuosity Factor | Replaces multi-gigabyte OpenStreetMap road network graph ingestions with five lines of deterministic Python math (![][image46])2. |
| **Transformer OCR (LayoutLMv3 / Donut)** | Tesseract OCR \+ Regular Expression Parser | Avoids downloading heavy multi-gigabyte neural weights and prevents GPU out-of-memory errors; extracts tabular weights and plates reliably. |
| **Deep Metric Learning Visual Deduplication** | 64-bit Perceptual Hash (imagehash library) | Computes in ![][image28]ms on standard CPU cores; identifies exact and resized image reuse across contract wards without setting up vector stores1. |
| **Live National Transport API (VAHAN)** | In-Memory SQLite/JSON Mock Registry (5,000 Records) | Eliminates external API key acquisition delays, third-party rate limits, and network dropouts during live judging demonstrations. |
| **Distributed State Machine (Temporal)** | Relational FSM Table with Database Transaction Locks | Implements an explicit state machine using PostgreSQL SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row locks; demonstrates state transition integrity without orchestration clusters. |
| **Distributed Headless PDF Cluster** | Local HTML-to-PDF Engine (WeasyPrint / Jinja2) | Compiles rich, multi-page audit dossiers with embedded CSS tables, discrepancy summaries, and base64 imagery in under 2 seconds locally. |

### **Hackathon Runtime Execution Trace**

> 1. **Submission**: The user accesses the web interface and uploads a test billing package containing an invoice PDF, two weighbridge scans, an MB scan, and four site photographs.  
> 2. **Synchronous Ingest**: FastAPI saves files to /data/artifacts/, inserts an entry into the claims table with state INGESTED, and enqueues a Celery task with the new claim\_id.  
> 3. **Background Processing**:  
   * *Normalization & Extraction*: Celery executes Tesseract OCR over the weighbridge dockets and MB scan, extracting net weights, volume dimensions, and vehicle plate strings. Concurrently, it extracts EXIF metadata from photographs and computes their 64-bit perceptual hashes.  
   * *Rule Evaluation*: The worker executes deterministic civil engineering formulas: it multiplies MB dimensions to obtain volume, computes expected mass bounds using ![][image47], compares the total against extracted weighbridge weights, checks vehicle plates against the mock SQLite registry, and checks photo GPS points against the PostGIS drain polyline buffer2.  
   * *Fusion & Scoring*: The worker computes a weighted anomaly score: any hard deterministic violation sets the risk score to ![][image48]; otherwise, an evidential combination algorithm scores image duplication and spatial variance12.  
   * *State Transition*: The claim state updates to ANOMALY\_FLAGGED if rules fail, or RECONCILED\_CLEAN if all checks pass.  
> 4. **Demonstration Interface**: The reviewer refreshes the dashboard to see the claim highlighted in red. Clicking the claim opens the Leaflet map showing where photos were taken relative to the drain corridor, alongside a side-by-side comparison of extracted weighbridge weights versus calculated MB volume limits3. An "Auditor Override" button allows the reviewer to input a sign-off comment and export a compiled PDF audit report immediately.

### **Production Infrastructure Subsystems**

* **Statutory Workflow Engine (Temporal Cluster)**: Manages audit claims as stateful, durable workflow instances. Temporal maintains execution histories, handles automatic retries for transient service failures, and manages long-running human review pauses (e.g., awaiting field engineer reinspection) without maintaining active database connection pools7.  
* **Event Mesh (Apache Kafka)**: Serves as the high-throughput ingestion backbone for continuous IoT data streams, including real-time truck GPS coordinates and automated weighbridge scale feeds. Telematics topics are partitioned by vehicle ID to ensure strictly ordered, in-sequence processing for route reconstruction2.  
* **Dedicated GPU Machine Learning Cluster (Ray Serve / Triton)**: Isolates deep learning inference from the core transactional workflow. Layout analysis models, convolutional vision backbones, and vector embedding extractors execute within auto-scaling worker pools that scale down to zero during periods of low submission volume, optimizing compute costs.  
* **Vector Similarity Store (Milvus / pgvector Clustered)**: Maintains historical collections of image perceptual embeddings indexed via Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs. Enables sub-second similarity searches across millions of historical municipal images to uncover cross-year, cross-ward image recycling fraud1.  
* **WORM Object Storage and Merkle Ledger**: Evidentiary files are committed to object storage with Object Lock enabled in Compliance Mode, rendering files physically immutable even against system administrator accounts9. System state changes, rule evaluation results, and human overrides are hashed into an append-only Merkle tree ledger, with daily cryptographic root hashes anchored to municipal external record systems to guarantee non-repudiation9.

## **Architectural Trade-offs and Core Design Invariants**

Enterprise architecture requires balancing competing operational qualities. MuniAudit-AI resolves four foundational trade-offs inherent to GovTech audit systems:

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

\+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
| COMPETING ARCHITECTURAL FORCES                   BALANCED PRODUCTION RESOLUTION                   |  
|                                                                                                   |  
| \[Deterministic Legal Rules\]                      Hybrid Gatekeeper Model:                         |  
|           VS.               \==================►  Deterministic rules act as strict filters;       |  
| \[Probabilistic Deep Models\]                      ML is confined to perceptual feature extraction. |  
|                                                                                                   |  
| \[Black-Box Neural Fusion\]                        Dempster-Shafer Evidential Reasoning:           |  
|           VS.               \==================►  Combines multi-source belief masses while         |  
| \[Dempster-Shafer Reasoning\]                      explicitly isolating conflict metric (k).        |  
|                                                                                                   |  
| \[Database-Polling Cron Jobs\]                     Durable State Machine Orchestration (Temporal):  |  
|           VS.               \==================►  Durable execution threads support pauses lasting  |  
| \[State Machine Orchestration\]                    weeks without maintaining open DB connections.   |  
|                                                                                                   |  
| \[Synchronous Gateway Proxy\]                      Presigned Direct-to-Storage Architecture:        |  
|           VS.               \==================►  Clients upload directly to storage, keeping      |  
| \[Direct-to-Storage Uploads\]                      API gateways stateless and resilient to memory.  |  
\+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

### **1\. Deterministic Rule Gatekeepers versus End-to-End Deep Learning**

* *Context*: Evaluating whether to build an end-to-end deep learning fraud classifier or a dual-engine architecture that combines deterministic business rules with perceptual ML models.  
* *Trade-off*: An end-to-end deep learning classifier can learn subtle, complex correlations across unstructured data streams. However, neural networks are vulnerable to adversarial evasion, suffer from uncalibrated overconfidence, and produce opaque classifications that cannot withstand legal cross-examination in statutory audit proceedings6. Conversely, hard deterministic rules are transparent and legally unassailable, but cannot parse unstructured image pixels or degraded document scans directly6.  
* *Design Invariant*: MuniAudit-AI establishes a **deterministic-first** invariant6. Machine learning is strictly confined to perceptual feature extraction (converting unstructured images into depth metrics, or scans into structured key-values)12. The core audit decision is governed by deterministic rules encoding civil engineering formulas, physical density bounds, and municipal municipal codes3. A deterministic failure acts as an unbypassable stop: no probabilistic model can override an arithmetic failure or a vehicle registration mismatch2.

### **2\. Dempster-Shafer Fusion versus Black-Box Neural Evidence Fusion**

* *Context*: Determining how to synthesize conflicting evidence streams (e.g., high visual silt removal confidence paired with missing weighbridge mass records and telematics speed anomalies).  
* *Trade-off*: Neural network late-fusion models can capture non-linear feature interactions, but they average out conflicting signals into ambiguous intermediate probabilities and require vast ground-truth training datasets that municipal corporations lack. Dempster-Shafer theory requires explicit definition of belief assignments, but provides a mathematically rigorous framework for handling partial ignorance and conflicting evidence12.  
* *Design Invariant*: The Multimodal Evidence Fusion Layer must execute Dempster-Shafer combination rules12. The system isolates the conflict metric (![][image18]). When sensors contradict one another, the system does not compute a moderate risk score; it classifies the case as an *Evidentiary Contradiction*, maximizes the epistemic uncertainty mass, and routes the dossier directly to a human vigilance officer with an explanation of the conflicting signals8.

### **3\. Workflow Orchestration Engine versus Monolithic Polling Schedulers**

* *Context*: Managing audit claim lifecycles that span weeks, require human-in-the-loop approvals, and involve complex multi-step compensation logic3.  
* *Trade-off*: Database-polling schedulers (e.g., cron jobs querying a relational status column) are simple to write initially, but introduce polling lag, race conditions under high concurrency, fragmented timeout handling, and unrecoverable zombie states when worker nodes crash mid-process. A dedicated workflow engine (such as Temporal) introduces an additional infrastructure cluster, but guarantees durable state execution, visual execution DAGs, and seamless handling of multi-week pauses7.  
* *Design Invariant*: Production deployments must isolate workflow state inside a dedicated orchestration engine. Audit claims are modeled as durable code workflows: activities handle discrete computational steps, timers handle statutory review escalation windows, and signals handle external human adjudication events without polling the operational database7.

### **4\. Direct-to-Storage Uploads versus Synchronous API Gateway Ingestion**

* *Context*: Handling the ingestion of multi-gigabyte billing archives containing hundreds of high-resolution images and PDF scans.  
* *Trade-off*: Routing file streams through the application API gateway simplifies authentication and request validation, but saturates gateway network bandwidth, consumes large amounts of application memory, and exposes the API tier to denial-of-service exhaustion during peak billing cycles.  
* *Design Invariant*: Ingestion must use pre-signed direct-to-storage upload protocols. The client requests an authorized upload ticket from the Ingestion Gateway; the gateway authenticates the actor, verifies file size quotas, and returns a short-lived pre-signed URL pointing directly to an isolated quarantine bucket in the object store. The application gateway processes zero file bytes directly, preserving its network capacity for interactive audit queries.

## **Prohibited Architectural Anti-Patterns**

A well-architected system must explicitly define the architectural anti-patterns, premature abstractions, and inappropriate technologies that are barred from implementation.

&nbsp;

| Prohibited Anti-Pattern | Root Structural Failure & Operational Consequence | Statutory Lean Architectural Alternative |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Public or Consortium Blockchains (Ethereum, Hyperledger)** | Extreme operational overhead, unpredictable transaction gas costs, low write throughput, key-management failure modes, and regulatory conflicts with statutory data modification or expungement laws. | Append-only relational database tables with SHA-256 cryptographic hash chaining, anchored via daily Merkle tree root hashes committed to WORM storage9. |
| **Autonomous "AI Judge" Payment Authorization Engines** | Direct violation of public finance statutory governance. Autonomous financial disbursement eliminates public servant liability, creating legal vacuums during anti-corruption prosecutions and introducing exposure to adversarial ML evasion8. | Human-in-the-Loop Adjudication Workbench: the system acts strictly as an evidential triage and decision-support engine; payment certification requires an explicit digital signature from an authorized engineer7. |
| **Monolithic Unstructured LLM Dossier Processing** | Hallucination of financial figures, non-deterministic outputs, context window token exhaustion, extreme per-claim API costs, and an inability to perform rigorous spatial or civil engineering mathematics6. | Strict separation of concerns: Layout-aware OCR extracts structured JSON data; deterministic code executes mathematical density formulas; LLMs are restricted strictly to generating natural-language text summaries of verified rule breaches6. |
| **Premature Fine-Grained Microservice Deconstruction** | Setting up 8+ microservices (e.g., auth, upload, ocr, rules, gis, reports) introduces distributed transaction failures, network latency, CORS bugs, and deployment paralysis, guaranteeing project failure in a hackathon setting. | In-Process Modular Monolith: strict domain namespaces within a single deployable artifact for the hackathon4; split only into high-memory/GPU worker tiers in production. |
| **Continuous Real-Time Streaming Video Telematics Pipelines** | Ingesting and processing continuous video feeds from thousands of truck dashcams or CCTV units requires massive network bandwidth, edge compute hardware, and storage infrastructure that exceeds municipal public works IT budgets by orders of magnitude. | Discrete Evidentiary Spatial Triangulation: High-frequency GPS breadcrumbs cross-referenced against static before-and-after geotagged photographs, weighbridge timestamps, and spatial geofences provide legally sufficient proof of work2. |
| **Proprietary Decentralized Identity (DID) Frameworks** | Introducing decentralized identity protocols for municipal actors creates unnecessary credential-issuance infrastructure, lacks administrative recovery paths, and conflicts with existing government personnel directories. | Standard OpenID Connect (OIDC) / OAuth2 federated identity providers connected to existing municipal Active Directory / LDAP employee backbones. |

The architectural integrity of municipal public works auditing rests on a non-negotiable principle: computational intelligence must never obscure public accountability8. By decoupling probabilistic feature extraction from deterministic civil engineering gatekeepers, MuniAudit-AI eliminates the primary mechanisms of desilting billing fraud—ghost haulage, photographic recycling, vehicle misclassification, and gravimetric fabrication—while preserving the legal transparency demanded by statutory oversight bodies1. The conscious progression from a lean, in-process Modular Monolith during rapid prototyping to an enterprise Workflow Orchestration Architecture ensures that municipal administrations deploy a system that is immediately functional within days, operationally resilient across decades, and legally unassailable before vigilance institutions7.
